subject: math
title: 2D Shapes and Symmetry: Sides, Vertices and Congruent Shapes
seo_title: Grade 2 Math 2D Shapes and Symmetry Worksheets: Sides, Vertices, Congruent Shapes (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Sort and identify two-dimensional shapes by comparing number of sides, side lengths, angles, and number of lines of symmetry
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on 2D shapes and symmetry for the Ontario curriculum: name shapes from triangles to octagons, compare sides and square corners, find lines of symmetry, put shapes together and take them apart, and spot congruent shapes. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count the sides to name a shape. Turning a shape does not change its name.
key_sub: A turned square is still a square, not a “diamond”. A line of symmetry makes 2 halves that match when you fold. Congruent shapes are the same shape and the same size.
body_html:
Sides and vertices

A 2D shape is flat. Count its sides to find its name. A vertex is a corner where two sides meet. Two or more are called vertices. A shape with straight sides has as many vertices as sides.

ShapeSidesVertices
Triangle33
Square4, all the same length4
Rectangle4, 2 long and 2 short4
Trapezoid4, only 1 pair go the same way4
Pentagon55
Hexagon66
Heptagon77
Octagon88

Turning a shape does not change its name. The sides do not have to be the same length.

Example 1

How many vertices does a hexagon have?

A hexagon has 6 sides. A shape with straight sides has the same number of vertices as sides.

Answer: 6 vertices

Equal sides and square corners

Compare the side lengths: are they all the same, or are some longer? Look at the corners too. A square corner (a right angle) looks like the corner of a book. The small marks show sides that are the same length.

Example 2

A square and a rectangle both have 4 square corners. How are they different?

Look at the sides. All 4 sides of a square are the same length. A rectangle has 2 long and 2 short sides.

Answer: the side lengths

Lines of symmetry

A line of symmetry cuts a shape into 2 matching halves. Fold along the line: one half lands exactly on the other. The line can go up and down, side to side or on a slant.

Example 3

How many lines of symmetry does a square have?

Fold it up and down, side to side, and corner to corner both ways. Each fold matches.

Answer: 4 lines

Put shapes together and take them apart

Small shapes can make a bigger shape. Big shapes can be cut into smaller ones. Pattern blocks are a good way to try this.

If you move the parts to make a new shape, it covers the same space. Nothing was added or taken away.

Example 4

6 square tiles make a rectangle. You move them to make a T. How many tiles are in the T?

Moving tiles does not change how many there are.

Answer: 6 tiles

Congruent shapes

Shapes are congruent when they are the same shape and the same size. One can be turned or flipped. Lengths are congruent when they are exactly the same length.

Example 5

Two squares have sides of 4 cm and 6 cm. Are they congruent?

They are the same shape, but not the same size.

Answer: no

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling a turned square a “diamond”Check the sides and corners: 4 equal sides and 4 square corners make a square
Counting a side twice, or missing oneKeep your finger on the first side and stop when you get back to it
Adding the sides of the partsCount only the sides around the outside of the whole shape
Any line that cuts a shape in two is a line of symmetryFold it: the halves must match exactly
Forgetting slanted lines of symmetryTry folding from corner to corner too
Saying a turned shape is not congruentTurning or flipping does not change the size or the shape

faq.q: What 2D shapes do Grade 2 students learn in Ontario?
faq.a: Grade 2 students sort and name triangles, squares, rectangles, trapezoids, pentagons, hexagons, heptagons and octagons. They compare the number of sides, side lengths, angles and lines of symmetry (Spatial Sense, expectation E1.1).

faq.q: Is a diamond a shape in math?
faq.a: No. A “diamond” is usually a square that is turned, or a shape with 4 equal sides that is not a square. Turning a shape does not change its name, so a turned square is still a square.

faq.q: What does congruent mean in Grade 2 math?
faq.a: Congruent shapes are the same shape and the same size, even if one is turned or flipped. Congruent lengths are exactly the same length (expectation E1.3).

faq.q: How can I help my child learn shapes and symmetry at home?
faq.a: Cut shapes out of paper and fold them to find matching halves. Use pattern blocks or cut squares into triangles, then move the pieces to make new shapes.

sets.title: Name shapes by their sides and vertices

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex and count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 5 vertices.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: Count the sides: 7 sides and 7 vertices. It is a heptagon. Count the corners that point in too.

items.q: A shape has 6 sides and 6 vertices. What is it?
items.e: 6 sides make a hexagon. 5 sides make a pentagon, 7 a heptagon and 8 an octagon.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: Count the sides: 5 sides and 5 vertices. It is a pentagon.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: It has 4 sides and 4 square corners. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex and count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 8 vertices. Count the small corners too.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: It has 4 sides that are all the same length and 4 square corners. It is a square.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: Count the sides: 5 sides and 5 vertices. It is a pentagon. The sides do not have to be the same length. It looks like a house, but it is one shape.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: Count the sides: 8 sides and 8 vertices. It is an octagon.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 vertices. It is a triangle. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: Count the sides: 6 sides and 6 vertices. It is a hexagon. The sides do not have to be the same length.

items.q: Which shape is a hexagon?
items.e: B has 6 sides, so it is a hexagon. The others have 5, 8 and 7 sides.

items.q: Which shape is a square?
items.e: A has 4 sides the same length and 4 square corners. It is a square that is turned. The other shape with 4 equal sides has no square corners.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side and count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 6 sides. Count the sides that point in too.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It has 4 sides. Only the top and the bottom go the same way (they are parallel). It is a trapezoid.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: Count the sides: 6 sides and 6 vertices. It is a hexagon.

items.q: Which shape is a trapezoid?
items.e: C has 4 sides, and only the top and bottom go the same way. It is a trapezoid.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 vertices. It is a triangle.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: It has 4 sides and 4 square corners. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It has 4 sides that are all the same length and 4 square corners. It is a square. It is only turned. “Diamond” is not its math name.

items.q: How many square corners does this shape have?
items.e: This shape has 4 square corners. Turning a square does not change its corners.

items.q: How many sides of this triangle are the same length?
items.e: The two slanted sides are both 5 cm. The bottom is 6 cm. So 2 sides are the same length.

items.q: Which shape has 3 sides the same length?
items.e: D has 3 sides that are all the same length. The other triangles have only 2 equal sides or none.

items.q: How many square corners does this shape have?
items.e: This shape has 0 square corners. Its corners are pointy or wide. None of them is a square corner.

items.q: Which 2 sides of this trapezoid are the same length?
items.e: The 2 slanted sides are both 5 cm. The top is 3 cm and the bottom is 7 cm, so they are different.

items.q: How many sides of this rectangle are 6 cm long?
items.e: The top and the bottom are 6 cm. The 2 short sides are 3 cm. So 2 sides are 6 cm long.

items.q: How many square corners does this shape have?
items.e: This shape has 4 square corners. They are square corners, like the corner of a book.

items.q: Which is true about this triangle?
items.e: The sides are 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. No two are the same, so all 3 sides are different lengths.

items.q: Which shape has no square corners?
items.e: C has 2 pointy corners and 2 wide corners. The others each have at least 1 square corner.

items.q: How many sides of this triangle are the same length?
items.e: All 3 sides are 4 cm. So all 3 sides are the same length.

items.q: A square and a rectangle both have 4 square corners. How are they different?
items.e: Both have 4 sides and 4 square corners. In a square, all 4 sides are the same length.

items.q: This is a square. One side is 5 cm. How long is the side on the right?
items.e: All 4 sides of a square are the same length. So every side is 5 cm.

items.q: Emma turns a square so it stands on a corner. She says it is now a diamond. What is it?
items.e: Turning a shape does not change its sides or corners. It still has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners, so it is still a square.

items.q: How many square corners does this shape have?
items.e: This shape has 2 square corners. The 2 corners on the left are square. The other 2 are not.

items.q: How many square corners does this shape have?
items.e: This shape has 1 square corner. The other 2 corners are pointy, not square.

items.q: Which shape has 4 sides the same length and 4 square corners?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners. A rectangle has 4 square corners, but 2 long and 2 short sides.

items.q: How many square corners does this shape have?
items.e: This shape has 0 square corners. All 3 corners are pointy, smaller than a square corner.

items.q: Which shape has 4 equal sides but no square corners?
items.e: B has 4 sides the same length, but its corners are not square. The square has 4 square corners.

items.q: A triangle has 1 square corner. How many of its corners are not square?
items.e: A triangle has 3 corners. 1 is square, so 3 − 1 = 2 corners are not square.

items.q: How long is the bottom side of this rectangle?
items.e: The bottom is across from the top. In a rectangle, sides across from each other are the same length: 7 cm.

items.q: Which shape has no lines of symmetry?
items.e: C has slanted sides that go the same way, so no fold makes matching halves. The square, the triangle and the rectangle each have at least 1 line of symmetry.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
items.e: Fold along the line: the left half lands exactly on the right half.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, it must go up and down.
items.e: Fold a rectangle from corner to corner and the corners stick out. The 2 triangles are the same size, but they do not match when you fold.

items.q: Which picture shows a line of symmetry?
items.e: A shows a line of symmetry: the top half of the shape matches the bottom half. The other halves do not match.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this shape have?
items.e: Fold it top to bottom or side to side: 2 lines. A fold from corner to corner does not match.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this shape have?
items.e: This triangle has 3 equal sides. A line goes from each corner to the middle of the side across: 3 lines.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this shape have?
items.e: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: up and down, side to side and 2 from corner to corner. Do not forget the 2 slanted lines.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
items.e: Fold along the line: the left half lands exactly on the right half.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, it must go up and down.
items.e: Fold along the line: the top half lands exactly on the bottom half. A line of symmetry can go side to side.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, it must go up and down.
items.e: Fold the square from corner to corner: the 2 halves match. A line of symmetry can be slanted.

items.q: Aiden folds a paper in half and cuts half a heart along the fold. Where is the line of symmetry of the heart?
items.e: When Aiden opens the paper, the fold is the line of symmetry. Both halves were cut together, so they match.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, it must go up and down.
items.e: Fold along the line: the slanted sides go opposite ways, so the halves do not match.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
items.e: Fold along the line: the 2 slanted sides are the same length, so the halves match.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, it must go up and down.
items.e: The top half is narrower than the bottom half, so the halves do not match when you fold.

items.q: The dashed line is a mirror line. The dot is 2 squares to the left of it. Where is the matching dot?
items.e: A matching dot is the same distance from the mirror line, on the other side: 2 squares to the right. 4 counts the distance between the dots.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this shape have?
items.e: Only the up-and-down line in the middle makes halves that match. The top is shorter than the bottom, so a side-to-side fold does not match.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this shape have?
items.e: This hexagon has 6 equal sides. 3 lines go through opposite corners and 3 through the middles of opposite sides: 6 lines.

items.q: Think of the flag of Canada. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Fold the flag down the middle: the red bands and the two halves of the maple leaf match. Fold it across and the leaf does not match upside down. So there is only 1 line.

items.q: Which picture shows a line of symmetry?
items.e: D shows a line of symmetry: the 2 halves match when you fold. The other lines cut the shape in two, but the halves do not match.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this shape have?
items.e: No fold makes the halves match, because the sides slant. It has 0 lines of symmetry.

sets.title: Put shapes together and take them apart

items.q: You put 2 squares of the same size side by side. Which shape do you make?
items.e: 2 squares side by side make a rectangle. It has 4 sides, not 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: How many triangles make this hexagon?
items.e: Count the triangles around the centre: 6. Each side of the hexagon belongs to 1 triangle.

items.q: Nathan cuts a square from one corner to the opposite corner. What shapes does he get?
items.e: A cut from corner to corner makes 2 triangles. A cut across the middle would make 2 rectangles.

items.q: Which shapes make this rocket?
items.e: The body is a rectangle. The nose is a triangle and there is a triangle on each side: 1 + 2 = 3 triangles.

items.q: Which shapes make this hexagon?
items.e: The top part is a trapezoid. The bottom half is cut into 3 triangles. 3 triangles cover the same space as 1 trapezoid.

items.q: How many sides does the outline of the whole house have?
items.e: Go around the outside: 2 walls, the floor and 2 roof sides. That is 5 sides, so the outline is a pentagon. Do not add 4 + 3 = 7: the line between the roof and the wall is inside.

items.q: Which shape covers more space?
items.e: Count the tiles. A has 6 squares and B has 6 squares. The same tiles were moved, so they cover the same space. B is longer, but it is not bigger.

items.q: Shape B is made from the 2 triangles of shape A, moved. Which shape covers more space?
items.e: B uses the same 2 triangles as A. Nothing was added or cut off, so both cover the same space. B is only wider.

items.q: How many square tiles make this shape?
items.e: Count each tile once: 3 going down and 2 more along the bottom. The corner tile is counted only once: 3 + 2 = 5.

items.q: Which shapes make this hexagon?
items.e: The line cuts the hexagon into 2 parts. Each part has 4 sides and is a trapezoid, like the trapezoid pattern block.

items.q: How many triangles make this square?
items.e: The 2 lines cross in the middle. Count the parts: 4 triangles.

items.q: Which two shapes make this house?
items.e: The wall is a square (4 equal sides) and the roof is a triangle (3 sides).

items.q: Which shapes make this square?
items.e: The line goes from one corner to the opposite corner. It cuts the square into 2 triangles.

items.q: Which shapes make this shape?
items.e: The line cuts it into 2 triangles. 2 triangle pattern blocks make 1 rhombus block.

items.q: How many triangles make this trapezoid?
items.e: Count the parts: 3 triangles. 3 triangle pattern blocks cover 1 trapezoid block.

items.q: Which shape is made of exactly 3 triangles?
items.e: D is a trapezoid made of 3 triangles. The others have 6 triangles, 4 triangles and 2 trapezoids.

items.q: Zoe moves all these tiles into one long row. How many tiles are in the row?
items.e: Moving tiles does not change how many there are. There are 5 tiles, so the row has 5 tiles. 3 counts only the steps.

items.q: How many parts make this hexagon?
items.e: Count the parts: 3. Each part has 4 equal sides. 3 of these pattern blocks cover a hexagon.

items.q: Which shapes make this rectangle?
items.e: The line in the middle cuts the rectangle into 2 squares. Each part has 4 equal sides.

items.q: Which square is made of 2 triangles?
items.e: A is a square cut from corner to corner into 2 triangles. The others are a square and a triangle, 2 squares, and 2 trapezoids.

items.q: Are these 2 shapes congruent?
items.e: The trapezoid is turned upside down. It is still the same shape and size.

items.q: Are these 2 shapes congruent?
items.e: A square turned is still the same square. Same shape and same size, so they are congruent.

items.q: Are these 2 shapes congruent?
items.e: The rectangle is turned. It has the same sides and corners, so the two shapes are congruent.

items.q: Which shape is congruent to “this one”?
items.e: C is the same rectangle, standing up. The others are a bigger rectangle, a square and a slanted shape.

items.q: Which shape is congruent to “this one”?
items.e: B is the same triangle, turned. The others are bigger or a different shape.

items.q: Are these 2 shapes congruent?
items.e: Both are triangles, but they are not the same shape. Only one has 3 equal sides.

items.q: Ethan cuts a square sandwich from corner to corner. What does he get?
items.e: A cut from corner to corner makes 2 triangles. They are the same shape and size, so they are congruent.

items.q: Jayden has a picture frame shaped like a rectangle. The top is 25 cm long. How long is the bottom?
items.e: In a rectangle, the top and the bottom are the same length. So the bottom is 25 cm too.

items.q: A window is a square made of 4 congruent small squares, 2 across and 2 down. Each small square is 30 cm on each side. How wide is the whole window?
items.e: 2 small squares go across. 30 cm + 30 cm = 60 cm.

items.q: Are these 2 shapes congruent?
items.e: One is a rectangle and one is a square. They are not the same shape.

items.q: Are these 2 shapes congruent?
items.e: One triangle is flipped over. Flipping does not change the sides or corners, so they are congruent.

items.q: Mei covers 2 hexagon blocks with green triangle blocks. How many triangles does she use?
items.e: 6 triangles cover 1 hexagon. 2 hexagons need 6 + 6 = 12 triangles.

items.q: Are these 2 shapes congruent?
items.e: Both are hexagons with equal sides, but one is smaller. So they are not congruent.

items.q: Mateo puts 2 congruent paper triangles together to make a square. How many sides does the square have?
items.e: A square has 4 sides. Do not add 3 + 3 = 6: the sides where the triangles touch are inside.

items.q: Are these 2 shapes congruent?
items.e: They are the same shape, but one is smaller. Congruent shapes must be the same size too.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. One has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. What are the sides of the other?
items.e: Congruent shapes are the same shape and size, so the sides are the same: 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. 6, 8 and 10 cm would make a bigger triangle.

items.q: A stop sign is an octagon. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: An octagon has 8 sides and 8 vertices. 16 adds the sides and the vertices.

items.q: Arjun sees a yield sign. It is a triangle with 3 equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does the shape have?
items.e: A triangle with 3 equal sides has 3 lines of symmetry, one from each corner to the middle of the side across.

items.q: Which 2 pencils have congruent lengths?
items.e: Congruent lengths are exactly the same length. 12 cm and 12 cm are the same.

items.q: Maya makes a quilt with congruent squares. One square is 10 cm on each side. How long is a side of another square?
items.e: Congruent squares are the same size, so every side of every square is 10 cm.
